_readme: Tunables and the deterministic first routing tier for scripts/triage.py, the act-loop. Where an alert,
an issue or a `warden run` goes is decided in this order: (1) `ignore` and the prose pre-filter close it
`ignored` with no model call; (2) the signal's LABEL picks the candidate repos: a native label (a Kuma tag,
a container name equal to a repo, an OTel `service.name`, the GitHub repo) first, then a `rules` match, which
is exactly a label route; (3) one sideclaw `triage` job runs for every item that gets that far and answers
attach | new(repo, title) | fixed_by | ignore, choosing among the label's repo or, with no label, among every
checkout with an AGENTS.md (it reads their `## Verify & Monitor` sections). `rules` is the tier a later wave
deletes once those sections cover the fleet; nothing else depends on it.
MATCH TARGETS. `rules`, `ignore` and `hostVerbs` are matched against TWO candidate strings per event, in
order, first match wins across BOTH: `source:external_id` (the raw form) and
`source:normalize_title(title)` (the human-readable form, normalize_title() from scripts/watchdog-poll.py).
For a grouped source (slack_alert, slack_update, hermes_log) the second form is fingerprint() of the title
(timestamps, ids, paths and ALL digits stripped, then normalized) and equals the first: write such a pattern
digit-free (`homelab-5m-load-above-threshold` is `homelab-m-load-above-threshold`; a truncated key ends in `*`).
For a state source (uk,
docker_homelab, docker_vps, op_refs_*) they differ: uk's external_id is an opaque UptimeKuma monitor id
('204'), so `uk:macmini-dev-host-push` (the title-derived target) is what makes that source matchable at all.
Matching is glob-style (Python fnmatch: `*`, `?`, `[seq]`), `rules` top to bottom.
`rules` is a list of `{"match": "<glob>", "repo": "<checkout under the repos root>"}`; the optional
`proposedAt`/`proposedBy`/`reason` keys are provenance only. The `evidence` key rules used to carry is gone:
the runtime-state probes it selected were deleted with the rest of that machinery (Wave 4 would have). THE
CONVENTION FOR WHICH REPO OWNS AN INFRA-SIGNAL ALERT: a RollHook-managed app's infra alert maps to the repo
that owns its COMPOSE FILE AND DEPLOY TARGET, not its source (`argo` is compose-managed inside `vps`, so a
downed argo container maps to `vps`); apps that deploy on every push to their own repo map to that repo; the
HyperDX-origin alerts map to `vps`, where their definitions live (vps/observability/alerts/*.json).
`ignore` (list of globs, or `{"match": ...}` objects) closes a matching item `closed(ignored)` before any
triage call. Use it only for a genuine recovery or a known-benign pattern you have looked at.
`minOccurrences` / `minOpenMinutes` are the one debounce: an alert is triaged once it has fired this many
times or stayed open this long. Issues and `warden run` are immediate. `cooldownHours` is how long a
signature that already had an investigation waits before it is triaged or investigated again, and how long a
`closed(ignored)` item that the triage model ignored stays closed after a recurrence before it gets a fresh look.
`quietResolveHours` closes a GROUPED item (slack_alert, hermes_log) that is still `new` and has produced no
occurrence for that long, to `quiet`. A `✅` recovery message in #alerts resolves a slack_alert item to
`quiet` at once. Neither ever claims a fix.
`ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse` (bool) is a structural pre-filter: a `slack_alert` item that no rule matched
and whose title does not start with a bot-alert shape (`[`, the siren emoji, a check mark, a warning sign) is
chat prose ingested from #alerts, and is closed `ignored` without a model call. It runs after `rules` on
purpose: a producer of bare sentences (Beszel) fails the prefix test on every real alert.
`hostVerbs` (list) lets warden run an idempotent host-level restart itself instead of asking the owner
(STATE.md, docs/history/state-log.md §59). Each entry is `{"match": "<glob>", "verb": "<key>"}`;
`verb` names a KEY of HOST_VERB_ALLOWLIST in scripts/triage.py, never an argv, and an unknown key drops the
rule at load. maybe_auto_remediate() also needs the item's own investigation verdict to rank at or above
`hostVerbMinConfidence` (high/medium/low, default medium). `hostVerbCooldownHours` (default 6) and
`hostVerbMaxAttempts` (default 2) bound repeats of one verb.
